t:
(a) 
The first paragraph of section 1384 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking out all of such paragraph preceding the word “whoever”, and inserting in lieu thereof: “Within such reasonable distance of any military or naval camp, station, fort, post, yard, base, cantonment, training or mobilization place as the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, or any two or all of them shall determine to be needful to the efficiency, health, and welfare of the Army, the Navy, or the Air Force, and shall designate and publish in general orders or bulletins,”.
 
    (b) 
The second paragraph of such section 1384 is amended by striking out the words “The Secretaries of the Army and Navy”, and inserting in lieu thereof “The Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force”.
 
    (c) 
The third paragraph of such section 1384 is amended by striking out the words “War or Navy Department”, and inserting in lieu thereof: “Departments of the Army, Navy, or Air Force.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Secretaries' power to "designate and publish" a distance resembles rulemaking or a joint consultative decision. But the only actors are the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, all federal officials, and publication in military general orders or bulletins is a one-way internal announcement, not a comment period or regulation involving outside parties. The section is a technical amendment adding the Air Force to an existing criminal provision, with no consultation, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: as the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, or any two or all of them shall determine to be needful to the efficiency, health, and welfare of the Army, the Navy, or the Air Force, and shall designate and publish in general orders or bulletins

qwen_block.w: This section grants authority to federal cabinet secretaries (Army, Navy, Air Force) to determine and designate restricted zones around military installations. The decision-making process is entirely internal to the federal government, involving only federal officials. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties such as the public, state governments, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: Within such reasonable distance of any military or naval camp, station, fort, post, yard, base, cantonment, training or mobilization place as the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, or any two or all of them shall determine to be needful to the efficiency, health, and welfare of the Army, the Navy, or the Air Force, and shall designate and publish in general orders or bulletins

opus.w: Only federal officials (the Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force) take part in deciding the restricted distance, and coordination between federal officials is not participation. Publishing the result in military general orders or bulletins announces the decision after the fact. It is not a comment period, a hearing or a consultation with outside parties. The rest of the section just updates wording to add the Air Force.
opus.s: as the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, or any two or all of them shall determine to be needful to the efficiency, health, and welfare of the Army, the Navy, or the Air Force, and shall designate and publish in general orders or bulletins
opus.b:
The tempting reading is "Yes": the section has several Secretaries jointly deciding something ("any two or all of them shall determine") and then publishing the result ("designate and publish in general orders or bulletins"). That reading fails on two counts:
- **Only federal officials are involved.** Coordination among the Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force stays inside the federal government.
- **Publishing is not participation.** Military general orders and bulletins announce a decision after it is made. They are not rulemaking and do not open a comment period.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants authority to federal cabinet secretaries to determine and designate zones around military installations. The decision-making process is entirely internal to the federal government, involving only the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force. There is no requirement or recommendation to consult with state/local governments, the public, or any other non-federal entities. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Within such reasonable distance of any military or naval camp, station, fort, post, yard, base, cantonment, training or mobilization place as the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, or any two or all of them shall determine to be needful to the efficiency, health, and welfare of the Army, the Navy, or the Air Force, and shall designate and publish in general orders or bulletins
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretaries "determining" a zone involves some form of consultation or decision-making process that could implicitly involve outside parties. However, the text explicitly assigns this authority solely to federal cabinet secretaries ("the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force"). There is no mention of consulting with local governments, the public, or any non-federal entities. The definition states that coordination between federal officials is not participation.
